what: S&P Global sells the ratings, indices, data and analytics that financial markets run on. It rates bonds, owns the S&P 500 and other indices, and supplies data on commodities, energy and the car industry.
customers: Asset managers, banks, insurers, exchanges, bond issuers, energy traders and carmakers.
money: financial data, desktop products and analytics
credit ratings on bond issues and issuers
energy and commodity price benchmarks such as Platts
the S&P 500 and thousands of other indices licensed to funds
data on vehicles and the car market, formerly IHS Markit
moat: Benchmarks that the whole market has standardised on: a bond usually needs two ratings to be sold, and index funds pay a fee to track S&P indices.
risks: Ratings revenue rises and falls with how many bonds are issued
Regulators periodically examine the rating-agency model
Index fee pressure as passive funds compete on cost
It is splitting off the Mobility business, which brings execution risk
opportunities: Index revenue grows with the money invested in passive funds, with almost no extra cost
Private-credit and sustainability data are new areas it is selling into
Separating Mobility can let both parts be valued on their own merits
watch: Bond issuance volumes, which drive the Ratings segment, and net new index assets.
